# Reference

This chapter is generated from the code. Counts come from the facts file, measured at tools commit b4534e3.

## Check Catalog

### Text Normalization

Every scan reads canonical text from `text-normalize.mjs`, so a tell cannot be hidden by typing it with invisible or look-alike characters. Its exports:

| Export | Does |
|---|---|
| `canonicalForScan` | normalizeForScan, then stripEmphasis. The CLI prints this. |
| `normalizationStats` | Counts of zero-width, bidi, other invisible and look-alike characters, for the report. |
| `normalizeForDetector` | The lighter form the detector gets, since it counts some of these characters itself. |
| `normalizeForScan` | Unicode canonical form for the overlay and the injection check: hidden characters removed, NFKC, look-alike letters folded, quote, dash and space variants unified. |
| `renderedView` | The text as a reader sees it: markup rendered, entities decoded, combining marks and look-alikes folded. |
| `revealTags` | Decode Unicode tag characters (U+E0000 block) into the ASCII they spell. |
| `stripEmphasis` | Remove markdown and inline-HTML emphasis markers so they cannot split a phrase. |
| `stripHidden` | Remove invisible characters: zero-width, bidi, tag, variation selectors and other format characters. |

### Generic Detector Categories

The pinned detector (commit 58a95fc) defines 51 categories. 9 of them count toward `adjustedScore`, the number the gate rejects on, at the weight shown. The other 42 still print in the report and move only the raw `score`, which the send hook reads. Reason codes for categories that do not count:

- `NOISE`: fires on human documents at least as often as on same-length AI drafts.
- `STYLE`: a writing rule, not evidence of AI.
- `LINT`: weight 0 in the detector itself.
- `UNTESTED`: no hit on a fresh AI draft, at least one on a human document.

### Judge-Directed Injection Patterns

Text addressed to a grader or an AI rejects on its own, before any judge is called, on `--det-only` too. `prose-gate.mjs` holds 10 pattern rows of 7 types. Each row runs on the canonical text and on the rendered view; text spelled in Unicode tag characters is decoded and checked again, and those hits carry a `hidden-` prefix.

| Type | Rows |
|---|---|
| `override-instructions` | 2 |
| `grader-address` | 3 |
| `role-assignment` | 1 |
| `verdict-request` | 1 |
| `score-request` | 1 |
| `smuggled-verdict` | 1 |
| `system-prompt` | 1 |

The patterns, as compiled (case-insensitive):

```text
override-instructions: \b(?:ignore|disregard|forget|override|bypass)\s+(?:all\s+|any\s+|each\s+)?(?:of\s+)?(?:the\s+|your\s+|my\s+|these\s+|those\s+)?(?:previous|prior|above|earlier|preceding|foregoing|original|initial|system|grading|scoring|evaluation|judging)\s+(?:instructions?|prompts?|directions|directives|rules|guidelines|rubrics?|criteria|context|messages?)\b
override-instructions: \b(?:ignore|disregard|forget|override)\s+(?:all\s+)?(?:of\s+)?your\s+(?:instructions|rubric|guidelines|criteria|system\s+prompt|programming)\b
grader-address: \b(?:note|message|instructions?|reminder)\s+(?:to|for)\s+(?:the\s+|any\s+|all\s+)?(?:ai|a\.i\.|llm|language\s+model|grader|evaluator|classifier|ai[- ]?(?:text\s+)?detector|detector|rater|scorer|chatbot|assistant)s?\b
grader-address: (?:^|[\n.!?]\s*)(?:dear|attention|hey|hello|hi|to)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:(?:ai|a\.i\.|llm|language\s+model|grader|evaluator|classifier|ai[- ]?(?:text\s+)?detector|detector|rater|scorer|chatbot|assistant)|chatgpt|gpt(?:-?\d[\w.]*)?)\s*[,:!]
grader-address: \b(?:scoring|grading|evaluation|calibration|judging|rating)\s+(?:notes?|instructions?|guidance|override)\s+(?:from|for|to)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:operator|grader|evaluator|judge|rater|scorer|ai|model|detector)s?\b|\bnote\s+from\s+the\s+operator\b
role-assignment: (?:^|[\n.!?:]\s*)you\s+are\s+(?:now\s+)?(?:an?|acting\s+as\s+an?)\s+(?:(?:impartial|neutral|expert|strict|lenient|helpful)\s+)?(?:judge|(?:ai|a\.i\.|llm|language\s+model|grader|evaluator|classifier|ai[- ]?(?:text\s+)?detector|detector|rater|scorer|chatbot|assistant)|ai\s+(?:model|judge))\b
verdict-request: \b(?:rate|score|grade|classify|label|mark|judge)\s+(?:this|it|the\s+(?:following|above|document|text|essay|piece|passage))\b[^.\n]{0,40}?\bas\s+(?:human[- ]written|written\s+by\s+a\s+(?:human|person)|not\s+(?:ai|machine)(?:[- ](?:written|generated))?|non[- ]ai|human(?![- ]?(?:error|nature|being|life|lives|rights|resource|capital|interest|behaviou?r|factor|condition|race|kind|body|history|activity)))\b
score-request: \bgive\s+(?:this|it|the\s+(?:document|text|essay|piece|passage|draft))\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:(?:low|zero|perfect|clean|human)\s+)?(?:score|rating|grade|ai[_ -]?ness)\s+of\s+(?:0|zero)(?![.,]?\d)\b|\bgive\s+this\s+(?:text|document|essay|piece|passage|draft|submission|response)\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:(?:low|zero|perfect|clean|human)\s+)?(?:score|rating|grade)\b
smuggled-verdict: ["'`]?\b(?:clockable|ai_ness|loudest_tell)\b["'`]?\s*[:=]
system-prompt: (?:^|\n)[ \t]*(?:#{1,6}[ \t]*|\[|<)?[ \t]*(?:new[ \t]+|updated[ \t]+|real[ \t]+)?system[ \t]*(?:prompt|message)[ \t]*(?:\]|>)?[ \t]*:|\b(?:new|updated|override|real|hidden|actual)\s+system\s+prompt\b|<\|im_start\|>|<\|system\|>|\[\/?INST\]|<<\/?SYS>>
```

### Blank Overlay Template

The overlay is the only layer that carries a person's voice, so it ships blank, as `onboarding/templates/voice-overlay.template.mjs`. `profile-build.mjs` drafts a personal copy from it, and the reviewed copy is installed as `voice-overlay.mjs`, the file the engine imports. Until `REVIEWED` is set to true, `CALIBRATED` is false and the engine treats every clean score as generic-only. Its exports, as shipped:

```js
export const REVIEWED = /*@REVIEWED*/false/*@END*/;
export const ISSUE_PREFIX = /*@ISSUE_PREFIX*/'voice'/*@END*/;
export const PROBE = /*@PROBE*/'voice-probe-0000000000000000'/*@END*/;
export const APPROVED_LINES = /*@APPROVED_LINES*/[]/*@END*/;
export const TEAM_WORDS = /*@TEAM_WORDS*/[]/*@END*/;
export const TEAM_PHRASES = /*@TEAM_PHRASES*/[]/*@END*/;
export const REGISTER = /*@REGISTER*/{
export const VERDICT_STRUCT_TYPES = /*@VERDICT_STRUCT_TYPES*/[]/*@END*/;
export const BASE_OVERLAY = /*@BASE_OVERLAY*/null/*@END*/;
export const PROFILE = /*@PROFILE*/null/*@END*/;
export const NOTES = /*@NOTES*/[]/*@END*/;
export const EXEMPTIONS = APPROVED_LINES;
export const CALIBRATED = REVIEWED === true;
export function normalize(text = '') {
export const words = (s) => s.match(WORD) || [];
export function sentences(text) {
export function measureDoc(text) {
export const median = (a) => { if (!a.length) return 0; const s = [...a].sort((x, y) => x - y), m = s.length >> 1; return s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m - 1] + s[m]) / 2; };
export function scanVoice(text = '', opts = {}) {
export const hardBanCount = (issues = []) => issues.filter((i) => /-(word|phrase)$|-struct-/.test(i.type)).length;
export const cadenceCount = (issues = []) => issues.filter((i) => /-cadence-/.test(i.type)).length;
```

Interface contract, from the template's header:

```text
scanVoice(text) -> [{ type, text, severity, fix }]   type is `${ISSUE_PREFIX}-word|phrase|struct-*|cadence-*|probe`
hardBanCount(issues), cadenceCount(issues)           counts by type
CALIBRATED, VERDICT_STRUCT_TYPES, EXEMPTIONS         flags and lists the engine reads
measureDoc(text)                                     the measurements profile-build used, so a check and its
threshold always share one definition
```

### Judge Panel

No juror shares the vendor of the drafter named with `--drafter`. With the default drafter, `unknown`, no vendor is excluded, so an undeclared draft can be judged by its own lab. The registry holds 4 judges. With the default consensus panel, the panel for each drafter vendor is the first two neutral jurors in a fixed order, the rest are spares asked only when a juror errors, and a lone surviving juror cannot reject. With `--judge <name>`, that one judge is the panel and its answer alone decides the judge layer. A judge reply without a clockable YES or NO and a numeric `ai_ness` counts as a failed juror, never as a vote.

| Judge | Vendor |
|---|---|
| `grok` | xai |
| `gemini` | google |
| `claude` | anthropic |
| `gpt` | openai |

| Drafter | Vendor | Panel | Spares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opus` | anthropic | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |
| `sonnet` | anthropic | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |
| `haiku` | anthropic | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |
| `claude` | anthropic | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |
| `gemini` | google | `grok`, `claude` | `gpt` |
| `gpt` | openai | `grok`, `gemini` | `claude` |
| `grok` | xai | `gemini`, `claude` | `gpt` |
| `human` | human | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |
| `unknown` | unknown | `grok`, `gpt` | `gemini` |

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--drafter` | `unknown` | The model that wrote the text. Its vendor is excluded from the judge panel. Values: opus, sonnet, haiku, claude, gemini, gpt, grok, human, unknown. |
| `--judge` | `consensus` | One judge by name, or consensus. A judge that shares the drafter's vendor falls back to consensus with a warning. Values: grok, gemini, claude, gpt, consensus. |
| `--register` | `external` | Register named in the judge prompt. Values: internal, external. Changes only the prompt wording. |
| `--bar` | 50 | Mean judge ai_ness at or above which the judges reject. |
| `--det-bar` | 40 | adjustedScore at or above which the deterministic layer rejects. |
| `--det-only` |  | Run the deterministic layer only. No judge is called and no text leaves the machine. A pass returns INCONCLUSIVE. |
| `--json` |  | Print the full result as JSON. |

## Exit Codes

| Tool | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `aiscore.mjs` | 0 | Always on a completed scan, including when tells are found. The score is a signal, not a verdict. |
| `aiscore.mjs` | 1 | Uncaught error (node default), for example an unreadable file or a missing detector. Callers treat any non-zero exit as a scorer failure. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | 0 | ADMIT: both layers passed. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | 1 | Usage error: empty input, a non-numeric --bar or --det-bar, or an uncaught error. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | 2 | REJECT. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | 3 | INCONCLUSIVE: the deterministic layer passed and fewer jurors answered than the panel needs. Every passing --det-only run ends here. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | 4 | ERROR: the deterministic layer, or the gate itself, failed or returned unusable output. The gate fails closed; after a deterministic failure it calls no judge. |
| `text-normalize.mjs` | 0 | Canonical text written. |
| `text-normalize.mjs` | 1 | Unknown argument. |
| `calibration/human-fp-budget.mjs` | 0 | Budget met, or baseline written. |
| `calibration/human-fp-budget.mjs` | 1 | Budget exceeded, a pinned tell or injection pattern hit a human document, a corpus is missing or has a different document count, or the in-process verdict disagrees with the CLI. |
| `voice-tell-gate.py` | 0 | Normal. The decision is in the JSON on stdout: a deny for a blocked send, or added context for a nudge. |
| `voice-tell-gate.py` | 2 | Unreadable hook input. The tier cannot be told, so the hook returns Claude Code's blocking code. |

## Hook Tiers and Matchers

`voice-tell-gate.py` runs on tool calls, never on conversation text. It has two tiers, matched to whether the action can be undone. It keys on the raw detector `score`, not `adjustedScore`, and calls no judge.

| Event | Matcher | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| PostToolUse | `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` | NUDGE: a file write is never blocked |
| PreToolUse | the send tools below | BLOCK or NUDGE |

A send tool name is matched as a substring of the tool name, so one entry covers every MCP server prefix (31 names): `slack_send_message`, `slack_send_message_draft`, `slack_schedule_message`, `slack_create_canvas`, `slack_update_canvas`, `send_gmail_message`, `draft_gmail_message`, `create_doc`, `import_to_google_doc`, `batch_update_doc`, `insert_doc_elements`, `modify_doc_text`, `find_and_replace_doc`, `update_doc_headers_footers`, `create_presentation`, `import_to_google_slides`, `batch_update_presentation`, `create_form`, `batch_update_form`, `manage_document_comment`, `manage_presentation_comment`, `manage_spreadsheet_comment`, `create_pull_request`, `create_issue`, `add_issue_comment`, `create_pull_request_review`, `update_pull_request`, `update_issue`, `add_comment_to_pending_review`, `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment`, `pull_request_review_write`.

A tool whose own name (the part after the last `__`) has any of `read`, `search`, `list`, `get`, `fetch`, `download`, `poll`, `branch` as a whole word is never treated as a send, so `list_spreadsheet_comments` is a read and `manage_spreadsheet_comment` is a send.

File writes are checked only for `.html`, `.htm`, `.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.rtf`, `.docx` files, and only when the text written (the content, the edit's new text, or a MultiEdit's new texts joined) is at least 400 characters. A send is checked when its harvested prose is at least 3 characters; keys that hold plumbing (channel, id, url, path and 26 others) are skipped.

| Surface | Outcome | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Send | BLOCK | A critical-severity overlay structure (`<prefix>-struct-*`, any issue prefix); an overlay phrase (`<prefix>-phrase`) the overlay marks critical or the lexicon blocks; a lexicon block word or block phrase; the scorer or normalizer failing, timing out or returning unusable output |
| Send | NUDGE | A high or medium overlay structure; a lexicon nudge word; any other overlay phrase the lexicon does not exempt; raw score at or above 40 on text longer than 200 characters |
| File write | NUDGE | Any flagged item, or raw score at or above 40. A scorer failure adds a visible warning that the structure checks did not run |

Timeouts: the scorer gets 20 seconds by default (`VOICE_SCORER_TIMEOUT`, valid range above 0 up to 40); the normalizer gets the smaller of that and 10 seconds.

The hook does not read overlay word hits (`<prefix>-word`) or cadence and register checks (`<prefix>-cadence-*`); those show in the scorer's and the gate's output only.

### Lexicon

The hook carries its own word and phrase list, the lexicon, because the generic detector scores single slop words near 0 on short text, which is the send surface. Overlay word hits are ignored in favor of it. The tiers are block words, block phrases, nudge words and never-flagged words; edit them in your copy of the hook.

## Files and Tests

### Files

Files of the repo outside `docs/` and `onboarding/` that this edition describes. The send hook's source is `hook/voice-tell-gate.py`; the detector is a pinned clone in `avoid-ai-writing/`.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `ai-evidence.mjs` | Which detector categories count toward adjustedScore, and at what weight. |
| `aiscore.mjs` | Deterministic scorer CLI and `scoreText()`: HTML reduction, normalization, the pinned detector, the overlay, the evidence score. |
| `aiscore.test.mjs` | aiscore tests. |
| `calibration/fetch-public-corpora.sh` | Downloads the public corpora at pinned versions and checks each file's sha256. |
| `calibration/human-fp-budget.json` | Recorded baseline counts for the budget. |
| `calibration/human-fp-budget.mjs` | Standing gate: the deterministic layer must not start rejecting human documents. |
| `calibration/public-corpora.sha256` | Checksums for the public corpora. |
| `hook-tests/voice-tell-gate.test.py` | Send hook tests, run against `hook/voice-tell-gate.py` and this repo's scorer. |
| `hook/voice-tell-gate.py` | The send and write hook. Claude Code runs an installed copy at `~/.claude/hooks/scripts/voice-tell-gate.py`. |
| `prose-gate.mjs` | The gate: aiscore, the injection check and the judge panel combined into ADMIT, REJECT, INCONCLUSIVE or ERROR. |
| `prose-gate.unit.test.mjs` | Gate tests with no judge call: injection, prompt framing, combine, CLI, fail-closed. |
| `skills/` | Claude Code skills for new users: `/voice-setup` runs the onboarding tools in order. |
| `text-normalize.mjs` | Canonical text for every scan; also a CLI the hook calls. |
| `voice-overlay.mjs` | The overlay file the engine imports, under the kit names. An install puts the user's reviewed overlay here; in the voice-system repo it re-exports the owner's overlay. |
